pairs.locus: Walter of Châtillon, Carmen I, stanza VI
pairs.question: Quid desertum nisi mundus?
pairs.answer: Mundus quidem set inmundus, quia munda respuit.
pairs.derivation: Authorial self-question opening stanza VI. Answer ends at the first full stop, after 'munda respuit'; what follows ('se desertus dici dolet...') turns from answering the 'what is the desert' question to elaborating the conceit, so it is cut.

pairs.locus: Walter of Châtillon, Carmen I, stanza VIII
pairs.question: Qui sunt spinae tribulique?
pairs.derivation: Authorial self-question opening stanza VIII. Answer is the direct identification; cut before 'cum non pascant set pascantur...' which digresses into the pasco/pascor wordplay rather than answering who the thorns are.

pairs.locus: Walter of Châtillon, Carmen I, stanza XI
pairs.question: Nam si pauper sit sophia, vilis erit: quare?
pairs.derivation: Self-contained rhetorical question with setup 'nam si pauper sit sophia, vilis erit' kept so the bare interrogative 'quare?' has its referent. Answer is the directly following 'Quia pauper ubique jacet'; nothing further in the stanza, so the answer is complete.
